note: Task-level set: real questions a person asks of this base, labelled with the minimally sufficient evidence. Unlike labelled-queries.json (built from filenames), these are written by hand and the expected path is checked by reading the note. A class of `absent` means the base should NOT answer; `ambiguous` accepts any of several; a task carrying `args` measures a documented flag, and `min_total` pins the width of the candidate set that flag implies. Every path in `evidence` or `accept` is graded 2 by `graded.py` (it answers); an optional `support` list names grade-1 notes, needed as support rather than answering, and it does not change the pass rule `tasks_eval.py` applies. A row with no `support` is a binary label, and `docs/research/task-set.md` names those rows and why.

rows.query: сколько стоит подписка Netflix в Таиланде
the exact number of stars on the 2brain repository

rows.why: The corpus holds only the singular `capsule`, in two notes: Evolver's Capsule (a gene plus one concrete case) and StatCraft's CapsuleCraft knowledge base. A plural query is therefore a pure word-form lookup, and the engine must retry the absent term as the form the index holds (c3c7ee4); `capsule` returns these same two notes, so a pass here means the plural costs nothing.

`exact` is documented as an AND of terms, not a phrase: every note holding both words matches, adjacent or not. The bitemporal note is the note about AS OF queries, so it is the right first hit; `min_total` pins the documented breadth, because a change to adjacency would still leave this note first while collapsing the 218 hits to the 7 that hold the literal pair. A phrase belongs to tb_grep, and this row is the line that says so.

This is the vault's answer for the oracle half of the oracle-matrix theme: run one test corpus against a live oracle in CI and diff the two outputs (the matrix half is absent from the corpus). Its body is Russian (korpus testov), so English `tests` cannot match there and `matrix` is absent; only `oracle` matches, which is below the default floor of two for a three-word query. The row states the expectation with no workaround, so it stays a probe of the floor.

The same note and query with the floor lowered to one: the note ranks third of 83, so the ranking does reach it once the floor stops excluding it. A pass here beside a miss on the default row locates the failure in the floor rather than in the index or the vocabulary.

rows.why: The English note says what the Russian question asks: every edge carries four timestamps, so validity in the world is tracked separately from ingestion time. There is no shared token, so the row measures the bilingual gap; the Russian sibling knowledge/bitemporal-valid-transaction-time.md ranks third and is a different note (the general model, not the edge model).
